newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Grain sees Q1 loss, profit in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Grain sees Q1 loss, profit in Q2.

text.p: Midwest Grain Products Inc said Thursday preliminary results for the September 30 first quarter indicate a slight loss.
President Ladd Seaberg also said second-quarter results are expected to show a return to profitability.

Scheduled for release in early November, final results for the company's first quarter are expected to show a substantial improvement over the prior-year's first quarter net loss of $2.4 million as well as an improvement over the fiscal 1996 fourth quarter net loss of $814,000, the company said.
"We are beginning to experience a turnaround and should move back into a positive earnings mode in the second quarter," Seaberg told stockholders Thursday at the company's annual meeting.
He attributed the turnaround to lower raw material costs for grain and strengthened demand for the company's fuel grade and food grade alcohol products.

"Prices for corn, milo and wheat, which we use in our production processes, have been trending down toward more normal levels recently, allowing us to significantly improve our operational efficiencies through greater utilization of our capacities," he said.
"Based on current conditions and our ability to significantly increase our productivity, I feel that we are well positioned to make considerable progress," Seaberg said.
